'''Royston Ricky Drenthe''' (born 8 April 1987) is a Dutch former professional [[association football|footballer]]. Although primarily a [[left winger]], he has also played as a [[left-back]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1152608.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100103094344/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1152608.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 3 January 2010 | title = Drenthe, the unlikely Galactico | publisher=FIFA | date = 31 December 2009 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref><ref name = "WF">{{Worldfootball.net|royston-drenthe|new_id=pe21783}}</ref>

Drenthe started his professional career with [[Eredivisie]] side [[Feyenoord]] in 2005, having graduated from the club's youth academy. He made 37 appearances for the side before switching to [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] in 2007. During his five years in [[Madrid]], he made 65 appearances for the club, spending time on loan at [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] and [[Premier League]] side [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], making 19 and 27 appearances for those clubs respectively. He then joined [[Russian Premier League]] side [[FC Alania Vladikavkaz|Alania Vladikavkaz]] in February 2013 on a free transfer, making six appearances in a brief spell at the club, before he joined [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in June 2013. In January 2015, he joined Kayseri Erciyessor, before moving to [[UAE Arabian Gulf League|UAE Pro League]] side [[Baniyas Club]] in September 2015. After being released by Baniyas in July 2016, Drenthe announced his retirement from playing. He has since begun recording music under the name '''Roya2Faces'''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-everton-winger-royston-drenthe-12577679|title=Ex-Everton man Drenthe becomes a YouTube rap star|first=Paul|last=Gorst|date=8 February 2017}}</ref> After two years, Drenthe came out of retirement to play for [[Sparta Rotterdam]] in 2018.<ref name="auto">{{cite news|url=https://www.ad.nl/nederlands-voetbal/royston-drenthe-naar-sparta-en-maakt-moeder-trots~ae7d42f3/|title=Royston Drenthe naar Sparta en maakt moeder trots|date=6 July 2017|access-date=6 July 2018|publisher=Algemeen Dagblad|language=nl}}</ref>

Drenthe made 17 appearances for the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands under-21s]] between 2006 and 2008, and was a member of the team that won the [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|2007 European Championship]]. He later made one appearance for the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands B]] team and also featured once for the [[Netherlands national football team|full national team]].

==Club career==

===Youth===
Born in [[Rotterdam]], Drenthe, who is of [[Surinamese people|Surinamese]] descent, joined local side [[Feyenoord]]'s youth system at the age of 13, playing mainly as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] during his junior years. After disciplinary issues during a trip to Switzerland with the B-side, coach [[Marcel Bout]] wanted him to leave the club, but the issues were resolved after the intervention of [[Rob Baan]], the club's [[director of football]].

Bout hardly used Drenthe in his subsequent lineups, and, at the end of the season, the 16-year-old was named as one of eleven players whose future at the club was questionable. He eventually moved to Feyenoord [[Farm team|feeder club]] [[Excelsior Rotterdam|Excelsior]].

Drenthe improved during the two years he played at Excelsior, with manager Marco van Lochem successfully playing him as [[left back]]. After impressing his former side's coaching staff, he was asked to rejoin the club, which he accepted.

===Feyenoord===
[[File:Royston Drenthe Feyenoord.jpg|thumb|left|upright|120px|Drenthe with Feyenoord.]]
In the [[2005–06 Eredivisie|2005–06 season]], Drenthe was promoted to Feyenoord's first team, managed by his former youth coach [[Henk Fräser]]. After scoring three goals against [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in the [[Otten Cup]] youth tournament he began training with the main squad, while still appearing for the reserves.{{citation needed|date=June 2023}}

In the same week where he helped his club to a 5–1 win at Ajax with the second team, Drenthe was offered a professional contract at Feyenoord. Manager [[Erwin Koeman]] handed him his [[Eredivisie]] debut against [[Vitesse Arnhem|Vitesse]] at the [[Gelredome]], and the player finished the season with three matches.

In [[2006–07 Eredivisie|2006–07]], Feyenoord signed veteran [[Belgium|Belgian]] [[Philippe Léonard]], while [[Pascal Bosschaart]] was also still part of the squad. After the former suffered an injury and the latter was transferred to [[ADO Den Haag]], Drenthe became first-choice as Feyenoord finished seventh in the league.

After winning the [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] with the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]], Feyenoord accepted a [[Euro|€]]14 million bid by [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] after Drenthe threatened to take his club to court if they did not want to let him go.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.as.com/articulo/futbol/Madrid/ficho/ayer/Drenthe/millones/dasftb/20070809dasdaiftb_29/Tes/|title=El Madrid fichó ayer a Drenthe por 13 millones|trans-title=Madrid signed Drenthe yesterday for 13 million|work=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=9 August 2007|access-date=22 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.abcgoal.com/news.php?type=transfer&no=559 |title=Real Madrid signs Royston Drenthe from Feyenoord |publisher=ABC Goal |date=9 August 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071014165330/http://abcgoal.com/news.php?type=transfer&no=559 |archive-date=14 October 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1202730233023/noticia/Noticia/Comunicado_oficial_2008-04-10_17:24:55.htm | title = Real Madrid y Feyenoord llegan a un acuerdo para el traspaso de Royston Drenthe | trans-title = Real Madrid and Feyenoord agree on Royston Drenthe transfer | publisher = Real Madrid | language = es | date = 9 August 2007 | access-date = 22 December 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130103131622/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/1202730233023/noticia/Noticia/Comunicado_oficial_2008-04-10_17:24:55.htm | archive-date = 3 January 2013 | df = dmy-all }}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
[[File:Roy-drenthe.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Drenthe with Real Madrid in 2008]]
Drenthe was presented as a Real Madrid player on 13 August 2007, alongside compatriot [[Wesley Sneijder]]. He made his official debut as a midfielder in the second leg of [[2007 Supercopa de España|the season]]'s [[Supercopa de España|Spanish Supercup]] against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], and scored the 1–1 equaliser from 40 yards out, with the ball hitting the crossbar and crossing the line. The ''Merengues'', however, lost 3–5 at home and 3–6 on aggregate.{{citation needed|date=January 2020}}

Drenthe played regularly for Real Madrid in [[2007–08 La Liga|his debut season]], in both left-wing positions, but began appearing less after the development of [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]], being dropped from the list of 18 by manager [[Bernd Schuster]] in several games. At one time, after being left out for the match against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], Drenthe stormed out of the training ground. He finished the campaign with 18 league appearances (plus four in [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|the season]]'s [[UEFA Champions League]]), scoring his first league goal against [[Real Valladolid]] in a 7–0 home routing on 10 February 2008. {{citation needed|date=January 2020}}

Despite rumours of him leaving the club on loan, Drenthe featured in 15 of Real Madrid's first 18 games of the [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 season]]. However, he also suffered from anxiety issues after being booed by the club's supporters during a 1–0 home win against [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] and did not feature for the club for a period, although manager [[Juande Ramos]] offered the player his support and insisted he would help him.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11835_4928429,00.html | title = Drenthe hit by anxiety | work = [[Sky Sports]] | first = Richard | last = Bailey | date = 16 February 2009 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> The manager later revealed that the player asked not to be picked for the three games after the Deportivo fixture.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sindhtoday.net/world/64510.htm |title=Real Madrid's Drenthe asking not to be picked due to anxiety |work=Sindh Today |date=16 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513023559/http://www.sindhtoday.net/world/64510.htm |archive-date=13 May 2010 }}</ref>

On 31 August 2010, after having appeared rarely in [[2009–10 La Liga|his third season]], Drenthe was loaned to [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] in a [[2010–11 La Liga|season]]-long move.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330013482321/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement:_Royston_Drenthe_loaned_to_Hercules_C._F..htm | title = Official announcement: Royston Drenthe loaned to Hercules C.F. | publisher = Real Madrid | date = 31 August 2010 | access-date = 22 December 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101211180051/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1330013482321/noticia/ComunicadoOficial/Official_announcement:_Royston_Drenthe_loaned_to_Hercules_C._F..htm | archive-date = 11 December 2010 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> He made his debut on 11 September in a 2–0 away win against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/48596/barcelona-vs-hercules/report |title=Barcelona 0–2 Hercules: Spanish newcomers stun Blaugrana at Camp Nou |work=Goal.com |date=12 September 2010 |access-date=22 December 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121127004502/http://www.goal.com/en/match/48596/barcelona-vs-hercules/report |archive-date=27 November 2012 }}</ref> and scored his first goal for the club on 14 November, netting from a free kick against [[Real Sociedad]] in a 2–1 home victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302080 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120721062442/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302080 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 21 July 2012 | title = Duo on song for Hercules | publisher = [[ESPN Soccernet]] | date = 14 November 2010 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> His performances with the [[Alicante]] team were subsequently praised by the Spanish press.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.elpais.com/articulo/deportes/madurez/Drenthe/elpepudep/20101116elpepudep_13/Tes | title = La madurez de Drenthe |trans-title=The maturity of Drenthe | language = es | work = [[El País]] | date = 16 November 2010 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> However, the player would soon fall out of favour with the club's board of directors and coaching staff after arriving one week after the winter break ended, citing a "loss of confidence in Hércules management", rather than what was previously perceived as "a protest over unpaid wages".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/primera/news/2011/01/07/LDE7061BU.php |title=Drenthe offers Hercules explanations after stay away |work=Reuters|date=7 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120712173123/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/primera/news/2011/01/07/LDE7061BU.php |archive-date=12 July 2012 }}</ref>

On 3 April 2011, in his second game after his suspension, Drenthe scored twice to help Hércules to its first away win since September, a 3–1 against Real Sociedad.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301825&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110408023846/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301825&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 8 April 2011 | title = Hercules claim giant win | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 3 April 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> He ended the season with 15 starts in 1,299 minutes of action, with his team being finally relegated. {{citation needed|date=January 2020}}

===Everton===
On 31 August 2011, Drenthe joined [[Premier League]] club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on a [[2011–12 Premier League|season]]-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/2011/09/01/blues-agree-drenthe-deal | title = Blues secure Drenthe deal | publisher = Everton F.C | first = Matthew | last = Gamble | date = 31 August 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> He made his Premier League debut as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in the 2–2 home draw against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], on 10 September. Again from the bench, against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], he scored in the 97th minute to round off a 3–1 home victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/premier-league/8765417/Everton-3-Wigan-Athletic-1-match-report.html | title = Everton 3 Wigan Athletic 1: match report | work = [[The Daily Telegraph]] | date = 17 September 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=318065&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120721014006/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=318065&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 21 July 2012 | title = Late goals lift Toffees | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 17 September 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref>

Drenthe made his first start for Everton on 21 September 2011 in a [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] match against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C|West Bromwich Albion]], [[Assist (football)|assisting]] the winning goal for [[Phil Neville]] in the 13th minute of [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] ([[2011–12 Football League Cup|2–1 home win]]).<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/331973?cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120717091812/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/331973?cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 17 July 2012 | title = Neville sinks Baggies | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 21 September 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> On his full league debut, at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on 23 October, he found the net just three minutes into the game in an eventual 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/317966?cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120719085042/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/317966?cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 19 July 2012 | title = Saha inspires Everton victory | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 23 October 2011 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref>

On 21 December 2011, after three weeks out of the game due to an [[ankle]] injury, Drenthe assisted [[Leon Osman]] for the game's only goal at home against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/16173159.stm |title=Everton 1–0 Swansea|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 December 2011|access-date=22 December 2011}}</ref> On 18 February 2012, in a match against [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] for [[2011–12 in English football|the season]]'s [[2011–12 FA Cup|FA Cup]], he scored after just 49 seconds in a 2–0 home success.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/338772?cc=5739 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120222080929/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/338772?cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 22 February 2012 | title = Blackpool rocked by quick-fire Toffees | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 18 February 2012 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> Drenthe started in the next game for Everton, scoring a powerful low drive from 20 yards out for the first goal of the 1–1 away draw against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11671/7571804/Distin-Drenthe-can-t-be-tamed | title = Distin – Drenthe can't be tamed | publisher = Sky Sports | date = 25 March 2012 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref>

In March 2012, Drenthe was given a leave of absence on compassionate grounds and, upon returning, he reported late for training. This resulted in manager [[David Moyes]] omitting the player from Everton's FA Cup semi-final squad; he was also told to stay away from the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/15/royston-drenthe-everton-real-madrid |title=Royston Drenthe told to stay away by Everton after discipline breach|work=[[The Guardian]]|first=Andy|last=Hunter|date=15 April 2012|access-date=27 April 2012}}</ref> Former Everton Goalkeeper [[Tim Howard]] confirmed that poor discipline and attitude around the club played its part in Drenthe being left out the squad. 
<ref>{{cite web | url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=DBDZSh-YVRY&feature=youtu.be | title=I Wanted my Team to LOSE! Tim Howard Talks About the WONDER Players at Man United &#124; Season 5 Ep #6 | website=[[YouTube]] }}</ref>

In a magazine interview published in April, he accused Barcelona's [[Lionel Messi]] of racially abusing him on more than one occasion, repeatedly addressing him as "negro".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18024212 |title=Barcelona dismiss claim Messi called Drenthe 'negro' |publisher=BBC Sport |date=10 May 2012 |access-date=21 May 2014}}</ref>

===Alania Vladikavkaz===
Drenthe left Real Madrid after his contract expired on 30 June 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/09/25/en/football/international_football/1348585432.html|title=Drenthe: from the top to the {{sic|nolink=y|'doledrums'}}|work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|date=25 September 2012|access-date=28 November 2012}}</ref> In December, he signed a deal with Russian club [[FC Alania Vladikavkaz|Alania Vladikavkaz]], which came into effect on 2 February of the following year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fc-alania.ru/press/news/alaniya_podpisala_kontrakt_s_rojstonom_drente|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130205070618/http://www.fc-alania.ru/press/news/alaniya_podpisala_kontrakt_s_rojstonom_drente|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 February 2013|script-title=ru:"Алания" подписала контракт с Ройстоном Дренте|trans-title="Alania" have signed a contract with Royston Drenthe|publisher=[[FC Alania Vladikavkaz|Alania Vladikavkaz]]|language=ru|date=2 February 2013|access-date=2 February 2013}}</ref> Drenthe made his league debut for his new team on 9 March 2013, against [[FC Rostov|Rostov]]. After the game, coach [[Valery Gazzaev]] called him a "great professional and an example for the youth".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/237353/Drenthe-voorbeeld-voor-de-jeugd-prof-met-een-grote-p.htm|title='Drenthe voorbeeld voor de jeugd, prof met een grote p'|trans-title='Drenthe example for youths, pro with capital "P"|work=[[Voetbal International]]|language=nl|date=9 March 2013|access-date=10 March 2013}}</ref> On 15 April, in only his fifth game for the club, he scored a [[hat-trick]] in a 3–1 home win over relegation competitors [[FC Mordovia Saransk|Mordovia Saransk]].

===Reading===
[[Reading F.C.|Reading]] officially confirmed the signing of free agent Drenthe on a two-year contract with the option of a third, on 21 June 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/drenthe-agreed-210613-875401.aspx|title=Royals agree Drenthe deal|publisher=Reading FC|date=21 June 2013|access-date=21 June 2013}}</ref> On 8 March 2014, Drenthe scored his first goal for the club in a 1–1 draw away at [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] after he cut in from the right and fired a left-footed shot into the bottom corner. Drenthe then scored his second goal for the club on 11 March in a 4–2 away win against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] with a free-kick just after half-time. In July 2014, Drenthe was told he could leave Reading after only one season with the club,<ref>{{cite web|title=Royston Drenthe to play no part in Reading FC's pre-season plans|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/royston-drenthe-play-no-part-7400472|website=[[Reading Post|Get Reading]]|date=10 July 2014 |access-date=11 July 2014}}</ref> whilst being stripped of his squad number when the official squad numbers were announced on 14 July 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Squad numbers confirmed|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/squad-numbers-confirmed-140714-1756693.aspx|website=[[Reading F.C.]]|access-date=14 July 2014}}</ref>

===Sheffield Wednesday===
Drenthe joined [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on a six-month loan on 1 September 2014, halfway through transfer deadline day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Transfer deadline day: Sheffield Wednesday sign Royston Drenthe|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29019413|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=1 September 2014|date=1 September 2014}}</ref> He made his Owls debut as a second-half substitute for [[Chris Maguire]] in the 0–0 away draw against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on 13 September. His only Owls goal came in the 1–1 away draw at [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on 1 November.

===Kayseri Erciyesspor===
On 23 January 2015, Drenthe joined Turkish [[Süper Lig]] side [[Kayseri Erciyesspor]].<ref name="Drenthe moves on">{{cite web|title=Drenthe moves on|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/royston-drenthe-kayseri-erciyesspor-reading-transfer-window-2222065.aspx|website=Reading F.C.|access-date=23 January 2015|date=23 January 2015}}</ref>

===Baniyas===
Drenthe joined [[UAE Arabian Gulf League|UAE Pro League]] side [[Baniyas Club]] in September 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Baniyas' newest signing Royston Drenthe hopes to 'play as well as Cristiano Ronaldo'|url=http://www.thenational.ae/sport/football/baniyas-newest-signing-royston-drenthe-hopes-to-play-as-well-as-cristiano-ronaldo|archive-url=https://archive.today/20151121120847/http://www.thenational.ae/sport/football/baniyas-newest-signing-royston-drenthe-hopes-to-play-as-well-as-cristiano-ronaldo|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 November 2015|website=The National|access-date=17 September 2015|date=15 September 2015}}</ref> He was released in July 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=El Trashico: Winston Bogarde, Thomas Gravesen and the Clasico's worst players| website=[[MSN]] |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/el-trashico-winston-bogarde-thomas-gravesen-and-the-clasicos-worst-players/ss-AAl2pRm#image=4|date=2 December 2016}}</ref>

===Hiatus===
Unable to find a club, Drenthe announced a hiatus from professional football, saying that he was 'no longer a footballer'.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/489458/royston-drenthe-real-madrid-retire-football-rap/|title=How Royston Drenthe went from star of the future at Madrid to the Dutch second tier|date=8 February 2019}}</ref>

===Sparta===
After training with the side for a few weeks, on 6 July 2018 [[Sparta Rotterdam]] announced they had signed Drenthe to a one-year deal.<ref name="auto"/> After [[Sparta Rotterdam]] promoted to the Eredivisie during the Keukenkampioen 2018–2019 season, the club decided not to extend his contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://nos.nl/artikel/2287056-gepromoveerd-sparta-heeft-geen-plek-meer-voor-drenthe-en-vijf-anderen.html|title=Gepromoveerd Sparta heeft geen plek meer voor Drenthe en vijf anderen|date=31 May 2019|access-date=31 May 2019|publisher=NOS|language=nl}}</ref>

===Kozakken Boys===
Drenthe then signed for Kozakken Boys.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49664141|title=Royston Drenthe: Former Real Madrid and Everton winger has 'no regrets'|work=BBC Sport |date=11 September 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Spain===
On 6 January 2021, Drenthe returned to Spain and signed with [[Racing Murcia]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=6 January 2021|title=Drenthe about to return to Spanish football|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/drenthe-about-to-return-to-spanish-football-936484|access-date=6 January 2021|website=BeSoccer}}</ref> On 30 January 2022, Drenthe was loaned to [[Real Murcia]], playing in the same city but a tier above Racing.<ref>{{Cite web|date=30 January 2022|title=Royston Drenthe jugará lo que resta de temporada en el Real Murcia|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-rfef/2022/01/30/61f6fb0a268e3ed56d8b45d0.html|access-date=8 February 2022|website=Marca}}</ref> In August 2022, he joined Racing Mérida City in the sixth-tier [[Divisiones Regionales de Fútbol in Extremadura|Primera División Extremeña]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Racing Mérida City|url=https://twitter.com/RacingMeridaCFC/status/1561750521827966977|title=¡¡Bienvenido!!|trans-title=Welcome!|date=22 August 2022|language=es}}</ref>

===Return to Kozakken Boys===
At the end of 2022 he returned to Kozakken Boys on a try-out.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.destadgorinchem.nl/sport/voetbal/880183/oud-international-royston-drenthe-keert-terug-bij-kozakken-boys | title = Oud-international Royston Drenthe keert terug bij Kozakken Boys |trans-title=Ex-international Royston Drenthe Returns to Kozakken Boys  | language = nl | work = destadgorinchem.nl | date = 29 November 2022 | access-date = 11 January 2023}}</ref>

On 17 November 2023, Drenthe announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/royston-drenthe-retires-real-madrid-everton-b1121159.html|title=Royston Drenthe, former Real Madrid and Everton player, retires from football: 'It's hard to swallow'|publisher=Standard Evening|language=EN|date=18 November 2023|access-date=19 November 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
After his first full season at Feyenoord, Drenthe was called by [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Dutch under-21]] coach [[Foppe de Haan]] to be part of his squad for the [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|2007 UEFA European Championship]], which was held in the Netherlands. He was one of the most important players in the second consecutive title of the competition for the ''Jong Oranje'', being chosen by [[UEFA]] as Player of the Tournament.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.uefa.com/under21/history/season=2007/goldenplayer/index.html | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120914092002/http://www.uefa.com/under21/history/season=2007/goldenplayer/index.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 14 September 2012 | title = 2007: Royston Drenthe | publisher=UEFA | date = 18 June 2010 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> The following year, he [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics|represented the nation]] at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{FIFA player|291376}}</ref>

On 14 November 2010, Drenthe was selected for the first time for the [[Netherlands national football team|Dutch senior team]], as coach [[Bert van Marwijk]] picked him as a late replacement for the injured [[Urby Emanuelson]]. Three days later, he made his debut, coming on as a second-half substitute in the 1–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win over [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].

==Personal life==
Drenthe's younger brother, [[Giovanni Drenthe|Giovanni]], is also a footballer. The [[striker (association football)|striker]] opted to represent [[Suriname national football team|Suriname]] internationally.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/news/newsid=692090/index.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110518192526/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/news/newsid=692090/index.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 18 May 2011 | title = Suriname's little secret | publisher=FIFA | date = 15 February 2008 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref> His cousin, [[Georginio Wijnaldum]], was another Feyenoord academy product.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/de/meldungen/royston-drenthe-der-zerplatzte-traum-vom-bling-bling-leben/blt259c6b0059d86b38 |title=Royston Drenthe: Der zerplatzte Traum vom Bling-Bling-Leben |publisher=Goal.com |language=de |date=20 December 2022 }}</ref> He is also the cousin of the Suriname international [[Tyrone Conraad]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.elfvoetbal.nl/binnenland/277202/interview-tyrone-conraad-het-is-heel-speciaal-om-met-royston-te-mogen-voetballen|title=Interview Tyrone Conraad: "Het is heel speciaal om met Royston te mogen voetballen"|website=Elfvoetbal.nl}}</ref>

Drenthe dated Spanish ''[[Playboy]]'' model [[Malena Gracia]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bild.de/BILD/sport/fussball/international/2009/04/30/real-madrid-star-royston-ricky-drenthe/liebt-sexy-nacktmodell-malena-gracia.html | title = Reals Star Heiße Affäre mit Nackt-Model |trans-title=Hot affair of Real Madrid star with nude model | language = de | work = [[Bild]] | date = 1 May 2009 | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref>

Drenthe recorded a [[Rapping|rap]] song with his friend [[U-Niq]] called "Tak Takie".<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hRn8k0HZb68 | title = U-Niq Feat. Royston Drenthe – Tak Taki Music Video | publisher = [[YouTube]] | access-date = 22 December 2012}}</ref>

In 2014, Drenthe opened a clothing store in Rotterdam with [[Michel Poldervaart]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ad.nl/buitenlands-voetbal/royston-drenthe-opent-eigen-kledingwinkel-in-rotterdam~adc4d833/|title=Royston Drenthe opent eigen kledingwinkel in Rotterdam|date=17 April 2014|access-date=11 November 2016|language=nl|publisher=Algemeen Dagblad}}</ref>

In December 2020, Drenthe declared bankruptcy after losing £3.2 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/799483/real-madrid-everton-royston-drenthe/|title=Former Real Madrid and Everton flop declared bankrupt aged 33 after losing £3.2m|date=4 December 2020}}</ref>

Drenthe has eight children from different relationships. In 2023 he started working in the healthcare sector, as he explained 'My entire family has always been in care'.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ex-speler Real shockeert bij Goedele Liekens: "Kunnen toch aan de pil?" |url=https://www.voetbalnieuws.be/offside/759443/exspeler-real-shockeert-bij-goedele-liekens-kunnen-toch-aan-de-pil |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=www.voetbalnieuws.be |language=nl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Former Real Madrid star Royston Drenthe reveals he is now a self-employed HEALTHCARE worker{{!}} All Football |url=https://m.allfootballapp.com/news/All/Former-Real-Madrid-star-Royston-Drenthe-reveals-he-is-now-a-self-employed-HEALTHCARE-worker/3066907 |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=AllfootballOfficial |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Mayo |first=Marc |date=17 November 2023 |title=Ex-Real Madrid ace Royston Drenthe retires from football: 'It's hard to swallow' |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/royston-drenthe-retires-real-madrid-everton-b1121159.html |access-date=11 April 2024 |website=Evening Standard |language=en}}</ref>

=== As TV commentator ===

Drenthe was contracted by the Spanish sports program [[El Chiringuito de Jugones]] as [[Sports commentator|commentator]], on 1 March 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/television/chiringuito-ficha-royston-drenthe-colaborador-11554009|title=El Chiringuito ficha a Royston Drenthe como colaborador|access-date=1 March 2021}}</ref>

== Health ==
In October 2025, Drenthe suffered a [[stroke]] and was hospitalised.<ref>{{cite news |title=Former Premier League star Royston Drenthe suffers stroke|url=https://news.sky.com/story/former-premier-league-star-royston-drenthe-suffers-stroke-13453579|access-date=19 October 2025|work=Sky News|date=19 October 2025}}</ref> His representatives confirmed he was receiving medical care, and former club Everton publicly wished him a speedy return to health.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Royston Drenthe: Former Real Madrid and Everton winger suffers stroke|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cz7peq9evywo|website=BBC Sport|date=2025-10-19|access-date=2025-12-02|language=en-GB}}</ref> In late 2025, his manager reported that he is undergoing rehabilitation and expressed confidence in a successful recovery.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Royston Drenthe: Ex-Real Madrid winger on course to make 'successful recovery' from stroke|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cdeg0n8npeeo|website=BBC Sport|date=2025-11-14|access-date=2025-12-02|language=en-GB}}</ref>
